guard_streams.source: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints revealed - Q1 2025
guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly complaint rankings are service-quality context and cannot establish selected-parcel broadband coverage, live orderability or measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q1 2025 complaints update on 7 August 2025.
The figures cover January to March 2025.
Overall complaints remained similar to the previous quarter.
Fixed-broadband complaints increased.
Pay-TV complaints increased.
Landline and pay-monthly mobile complaint levels stayed the same.
TalkTalk was the most complained-about broadband provider.
Plusnet generated the fewest broadband complaints.
EE and TalkTalk were the most complained-about landline providers.
Utility Warehouse generated the fewest landline complaints.

guard_streams.source: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints revealed - Q2 2025
guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly complaint rankings are service-quality context and cannot establish selected-parcel broadband coverage, live orderability or measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q2 2025 complaints update on 6 November 2025.
The figures cover April to June 2025.
Overall complaints decreased compared with the previous quarter.
Broadband complaints decreased.
Landline complaints decreased.
Pay-monthly mobile complaints decreased.
Pay-TV complaint levels remained unchanged.
TalkTalk generated the highest broadband complaint rate.
Plusnet generated the lowest broadband complaint rate.
O2 generated the highest pay-monthly mobile complaint rate.

guard_streams.write_limit: Complaint-volume reporting supports provider comparison but does not verify parcel-level network availability, orderability or measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom first published the complaints report page on 27 July 2011.
The report page was updated on 23 July 2026.
Ofcom publishes provider complaint data quarterly.
The report includes providers meeting the relevant market-share threshold.
It covers broadband, landline, pay-monthly mobile and pay-TV services.
Complaint volumes are normalised per 100,000 subscribers.
The figures concern complaints made directly to Ofcom.
They do not represent every complaint received by providers.
The publication helps consumers compare provider service quality.
The page provides supporting data downloads and reports.

guard_streams.write_limit: Programme evaluation design, questions and methods do not establish current selected-parcel serviceability or measured broadband speed.

facts.detail: The Project Gigabit Evaluation Plan was published on 22 December 2022.
The plan sets out evaluation of the Project Gigabit programme.
It includes process, impact and value-for-money evaluation.
The evaluation is structured around a programme theory of change.
Impact evaluation considers counterfactual analysis.
Evidence sources include administrative and survey data.
The evaluation is designed to run over multiple years.
It examines connectivity, economic and social outcomes.
The plan covers multiple Project Gigabit intervention routes.
Evaluation evidence is not a live premises-orderability test.

guard_streams.source: Local Full Fibre Networks Programme Evaluation Plan
guard_streams.write_limit: Evaluation design for public investment cannot establish current selected-parcel broadband coverage, orderability or measured speed.

facts.detail: The LFFN Evaluation Plan was published on 29 October 2020.
It covers the Local Full Fibre Networks programme.
The programme aimed to stimulate commercial full-fibre investment.
It includes public-sector connectivity interventions.
The evaluation includes process, impact and value-for-money strands.
The plan uses a theory-of-change framework.
Monitoring, survey and administrative evidence are included.
The plan considers business and local-economy outcomes.
Potential network spillover effects are part of the evaluation.
Programme evaluation is not live parcel-service evidence.
